## Setup

### Packages

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# check if need both tidyverse and ggplot2
# janitor and DataExplorer are good for data wrangling 
packages = c("tidyverse", "janitor", "DataExplorer")


packageCheck = function(x) {
    if (!require(x, character.only = TRUE)) {
      install.packages(x, dependencies = TRUE)
      library(x, character.only = TRUE)
    }
  }

## Now load or install & load all
loadPacks<-lapply(packages, packageCheck)
```

## Define function to produce plots
One function (for submission 2)
```{r}
# can we also do this for submission 1
# can we have one central function that calls each of three functions for making three different plots
# for geneNames, don't need to tell function it's a list but use [[]] to get things from in it 
create_plot <- function(df, geneName, contCov, catCov1, catCov2){
  
}

create_histogram <- function(df, geneName){
  # x is gene expression 
  ggplot(df, aes()) +
    geom_histogram() + 
    labs(
      
    )
}

create_scatterplot <- function(df, geneName, contCov){
  # x is covariate, y is gene expression
  ggplot(df, aes(x = contCov)) + 
    geom_point() +
    labs(
      x = geneName,
      y = contCov
    )
}

create_boxplot <- function(df, geneName, catCov1, catCov2){
  # join catCov1 and catCov2 to get all possible combinations of both
  # this will be interesting for naming
  # OR could do faceting for one 
  # actually color will help with this too
  
  # x is gene exp, y is both categorical variables 
  ggplot(df, aes(x = df[geneName], y = catCov1, color = catCov2)) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    labs(
      x = geneName,
      y = catCov1,
      color = catCov2
    )
}

# function to create all of three plots for each gene name given 
# might need to pass in theme value? but that's as a function call so not quite sure how that will work
# will want to be able to easily change theme and have it apply to all plots 
create_plots <- function(df, geneNames, contCov, catCov1, catCov2){
  apply(geneNames, create_plot) # so actually this will probably not work bc too many inputs going on
  # double check if inputs are the values or labels or categories or what 
  
  # define iterator 
  i <- 1
  # for i in geneNames make each set of plots 
  # maybe only pass in the relevant part of the data frame ? 
  #   say, create new df with just the input gene name
  # make histogram of gene exp
  create_histogram(df, geneName[i])
  
  # make scatterplot cov vs gene exp
  create_scatterplot(df, geneName[i], contCov)

  # make boxplot gene exp w both cov 
  create_boxplot(df, geneName[i], catCov1, catCov2)
}

```
